question: If $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ is defined by $f(n) = \begin{cases} \frac{n+1}{2}, & \text{if } n \text{ is odd} \\ \frac{n}{2}, & \text{if } n \text{ is even} \end{cases}$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$. State whether the function $f$ is bijective. Justify your answer.
explanation:
Check injectivity: $f(1) = \frac{1+1}{2} = 1$ and $f(2) = \frac{2}{2} = 1$. Thus $f(1) = f(2)$ but $1 \ne 2$. Hence the function is not one-one.

Check surjectivity: For any $m \in \mathbb{N}$, if we take $n = 2m-1$ then $f(n) = m$. Also if we take $n = 2m$ then $f(n) = m$. Thus every natural number has a pre-image.

Hence $f$ is onto but not one-one.

Therefore $f$ is not bijective.

options.A: $f$ is one-one and onto, so it is bijective
options.B: $f$ is one-one but not onto, so it is not bijective
options.C: $f$ is onto but not one-one, so it is not bijective
